Hi Kyle / OrbitEdge SRE team —

Thanks again for lining up the dedicated commitment. Before we schedule a hard cutover, we want to run a short verification + warm-swap rehearsal to validate sizing, tail latency, and our rollback signals. Proposed scope: 

- Performance validation on a reserved staging pool (same GPU types as production) — synthetic and sampled production traffic
- 99th and 99.9th P99 latency checks, token throughput validation, and KV cache hit sanity checks
- One rehearsal dry-run of traffic shift (warm handoff) with controlled ramp and rollback window

Tentative dates: validation run July 8–9; rehearsal window July 13 (UTC-friendly window). Please confirm if those dates work for you.

Attached: oe_baseline_throughput.csv — our initial request-derived baseline (sampled over last 7 days from Hosted).

Action items I want to lock this week:
- OrbitEdge: confirm traffic shape and important latency SLAs (p95/p99 targets)
- Redwood: finalize test cases and runbook owners
- Procurement: confirm DocuSign readiness for the dedicated contract (we can still rehearse before signature if you prefer)

Thanks — I’ll schedule an internal runbook walkthrough with Ben & Kim once we confirm dates.

Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference

Chloe / Kim —

Internal plan draft for the validation run (high level):

1) Test bed: allocate 4x A100-equivalent instances in staging with identical runtime config and model variant (quant/profile as production).
2) Test cases:
   - Baseline steady-state at 1k RPS (5m buckets) — measure token throughput and per-token cost
   - Burst test at 4k RPS sustained for 120s — capture P95/P99/P99.9
   - Long-context stress: 8k-token sessions (sampled) to validate KV cache behavior
   - Cache warmup: repeated prefix hits to measure impact on tail latency
3) Observability hooks: tracing enabled, token-level breakdowns, and runbook alert thresholds pre-configured (latency > 2.5s P99.9 triggers immediate rollback).
4) Owners: Ben — perf harness & synthetic generation; Kim — tracing and dashboards; Chloe — customer coordination & acceptance gates.

Questions for OrbitEdge before we run:
- Confirm token distribution (avg tokens / session, 90th, 99th) and top-10 prompt families.
- Any request shaping (client-side retries or batching) we should mirror?

I’ll provision the staging nodes July 6 and run a dry smoke test July 7.

Ben
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

(on a related note — we should add the rehearsal checklist to the MAP doc Chloe is assembling)

Subject: Re: OrbitEdge — Dedicated capacity verification & warm swap rehearsal — rehearsal summary & go/no-go

Team —

Summary from the rehearsal today (July 14):

- Smoke & perf tests: all pass at steady 1k RPS. Burst test to 4k RPS for 2 minutes showed P99.9 = 2.3s (under the 2.5s threshold). KV cache warmed as expected; cache hit rate climbed from 28% to 71% during repeated prefixes.
- Rehearsal traffic shift: gradual ramp (0% -> 60% -> 100% traffic) over 25 minutes — handoff proceeded without SLO breaches.
- Observability: tracing and token-level breakdowns captured; we found one alert threshold that was too sensitive (noise around short tail spikes). Ben will tune the alert to avoid false positives during next-minute bursts.

Go/No-go recommendation: GO for a controlled cutover window. Proposed production swap window: July 20, 02:00–05:00 UTC (we recommend a 3-hour window for ramp + validation). Rollback plan: immediate manual rollback + automated throttle if P99.9 > 2.5s for two consecutive 5-minute buckets.

Open items before cutover:
- OrbitEdge: confirm final procurement signature / PO by July 19 EOD
- Redwood: Ben to tune noisy alert (ETA July 15), Kim to publish the runbook and escalation matrix (ETA July 16)
- All: one final smoke run on July 19 22:00 UTC to validate production config

Attachments: rehearsal_runlog.zip (zip, 2.1MB) — contains raw traces, run logs, and the final rehearsal metrics CSV.

Thanks everyone — great coordination. We’ll convert the MAP to a cutover checklist and loop in CS for post-cutover monitoring.

Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

(If anything changes on procurement timing @Procurement Team at OrbitEdge, flag immediately so we can postpone the window.)
